reflection.text:
Unblinded as methotrexate - ChEMBL CHEMBL34259 Dihydrofolate reductase inhibitor, PubChem CID 126941, identity check name and BBBC021 structure agree. Submitted conclusion DNA replication (p=0.38) was correct. Verdict approve is justified.

What the evidence got right:

- Phenotype was strikingly consistent across all 4 wells sampled at 0.1, 0.3, 1 and 10 uM (e2, e3, e6, e7): nuc_dna_mean z = -10.1 to -11.9, cell_area z = +5.6 to +7.7, nuc_dna_integrated -2.6 to -3.2, and cell_major_axis/nuc_major_axis increased. This is DNA mean dilution with large spread cells and lower density vs DMSO on visual review (e4), without cytoskeletal collapse - tub_mean z only ~-1 to -1.8 and act_mean not collapsed (e13, e14 rho -0.40 p=0.6), and microscopist noted preserved tubulin/actin visually intact. This correctly excluded Actin disruptors, Microtubule destabilizers/stabilizers, Aurora and Eg5 inhibitors which were in the broad visual differential (e4) but contradicted by e2, e4, e11 frac_mitotic_like suppressed and e13 tub_mean flat.

- Classification as S-phase/antimetabolite block fits the on-target effect of DHFR inhibition depleting reduced folates for thymidylate/purine synthesis. PMID 1175648 documents DNA replication in methotrexate-treated human lymphoblasts, and PMID 22049385 and PMID 26433846 review methotrexate/antimetabolites as DNA replication inhibitors. The enlarged flattened nuclei and increased cell area with decreased DNA concentration are consistent with megaloblastic-type S-phase arrest described for antifolates, e.g. drug-induced megaloblastic change PMID 6450011, not seen with this title alone without over-interpreting z-scores as specific megaloblastosis.

- Atlas comparison (e5) correctly gave plurality to DNA replication 4/10 vs Kinase inhibitors 3/10 vs Microtubule destabilizers 1/10, mean 0.635 vs 0.589. Setting hypotheses to DNA replication 0.38 > Kinase 0.22 > DNA damage 0.15 was appropriately modest given weak similarity and non-specific large-cell phenotype noted in e4 and in review critique. Probability 0.38 was not overstated.

What misled or was missing and why:

- Acquisition strategy sampled only the plateau. e1 offered 8 doses 0.003-10 uM with budget 4 wells, and we sampled dose 7 (10 uM), dose 5 (1 uM), dose 3 (0.1 uM) and dose 4 (0.3 uM). All were already maximal, so dose_response rho for nuc_dna_mean +0.40 p=0.6 (e8), cell_area +0.20 p=0.8 (e9), cell_count +0.40 p=0.6 (e10), nuc_area -0.40 p=0.6 (e12) and tub_mean 0.00 p=1 (e13) were all non-significant. This was not lack of dose-dependence but sampling the wrong window; we never acquired 0.003-0.03 uM to define EC50, as noted in our own next-experiment proposal.

- Visual describe_phenotype (e4) returned 5 observations spanning Actin, Microtubule, Aurora, Eg5 and DNA damage - a default large-cell differential that was too broad. Quantitative features were needed to downweight cytoskeletal/motor classes.

- Atlas similarity was weak and close between top classes, so DNA damage vs DNA replication could not be separated on morphology alone in 4 fields. We correctly kept DNA damage as second-tier hypothesis (0.15) but had no orthogonal EdU pulse, p-H2AX/p53, or washout to distinguish pure S-phase block from DNA damage response or senescence-like G1 hypertrophy.

Lesson: For antifolates the morphologic signature is plateaued DNA dilution + hypertrophy + mitotic suppression with preserved cytoskeleton. Future runs should spend 1-2 wells on the low-dose threshold (0.003-0.03 uM here) to capture EC50 and add EdU and p-H2AX to separate DNA replication inhibition from DNA damage and kinase-induced hypertrophy, rather than re-sampling the plateau.
